From Long Island, take the LIRR to Atlantic Terminal then take the D, N or R train to 36th street.
More About Half Step
Half Step is a group of dedicated fans & students of the Grateful Dead, capturing the spirit, improvisation, sound & complexity of Grateful Dead music. Established in 2004 on Long Island, Half Step has been mastering their craft while winning over crowds of veteran Deadheads, newcomers and non-Dead fans alike.
What makes Half Step stand out from the rest?
Like the Grateful Dead themselves, the band is constantly pushing the envelope, growing together as musicians and performers. Only true fans that have experienced and studied the music with an extreme level of dedication and passion can accurately represent the superb body of work that the Grateful Dead have to offer.
When seeing Half Step live, one can clearly see the attention to detail that the band has in putting on a viable Grateful Dead experience. They stay true to the traditional show format and play sets of tunes in a sequence that could likely have been performed by the Dead themselves years ago. The members of Half Step also use similar instruments, amplifiers and effects to further authenticate the Grateful Dead sound.
In the band’s long history, they have undergone and overcome numerous incarnations. With each new member they come closer to refining their approach while consistently raising their standards. Half Step’s current line up is by far the most seasoned and prepared to bring their show to the next level.
As musicians, Half Step has what it takes to present the Dead’s music to even the most critical of fans. Anyone who has experienced the Grateful Dead in one way or another have formed a unique impression of their music. Half Step has the rare privilege to be in the position to share their collective impression with you.

This is a one day in person seminar from 10am to 5pm with a 1 hour lunch break.
Level up your service skills in sake! This one day sake training certification course will teach you all the ins and outs of proper service and sales for sake in your your restaurant or retail shop. There is no prerequisite and this course is open to anyone wishing to get training in professional service of sake. The course consists of four modules.

2) sake sales techniques
3) sake service and presentation
4) sake menus and pairing

events.title: Sake Revolution LIVE! Featuring Austin Power
events.description:
October 1st is Sake Day — the official start of the sake brewing year in Japan. And every year on the day itself, Sake Revolution, America’s first sake podcast, keeps its favorite tradition: recording a live episode in front of an audience at the Brooklyn Kura Taproom. The kanpai is mandatory… but fun will be inevitable.
We couldn’t be more excited about this year’s guest: Austin Power (yes, that’s his real name), New York’s most seriously silly sake sommelier and the man behind Accidental Bar, downtown’s beloved neighborhood sake joint on Avenue C.
A South Carolina kid turned Parsons-trained painter turned sake evangelist, his mission has been, in his own words, “get more people drinking more sake, more irresponsibly” and “if you’re not having fun, you’re doing it wrong”. He honed that philosophy over a decade at legendary NYC sake spots before opening Accidental Bar in 2021.
Join hosts John and Timothy as they talk to Austin about his take on the sake scene in NYC!

Come for the party, Leave a little Smarter – we dive into Austin’s philosophy of how to get more people drinking more sake, more irresponsibly and what is the best path forward with the staid and serious world of “Sake Education”
The State of Sake in NYC — real talk on trends, challenges, and bright spots from the sake-selling trenches of NYC – how the NYC sake scene grew from a handful of pioneers into one of the best sake-drinking towns outside Japan.

Fair warning: an evening with Austin is entertainment, full stop. Less lecture, more live show — equal parts tasting, talk show, and party. You’ll laugh, you’ll sip, and somewhere along the way you’ll accidentally learn a lot about sake.
Your ticket includes a tasting flight hand-picked by Austin himself — Accidental Bar favorites, poured and tasted together during the recording. And bring your questions: we collect written questions from the audience during the show, and our live audience Q&A segment is always a highlight of the episode.
Come early for happy hour, stay late at the taproom bar, and celebrate Sake Day the only correct way: glass in hand, with friends. Because as Austin says — “If I can see you, aren’t we already friends?!”
Seats are limited (this one always fills up). Kanpai Ya’ll!
events.vendor: Sake Revolution LIVE! Featuring Austin Power

CiderFeast Brooklyn brings together the region’s best cideries and perfectly pairs pours of hard cider with outstanding bites from neighborhood favorites.
This year’s lineup features nationally recognized ciders as well as producers whose work is rooted in the region’s distinctive fruit and terroir, including:
1911 Established
Atomic Dog Ciders
Aval Cider
Eden Ciders
Frosty Twig Cider
Indian Ladder Farms Cidery & Brewery
Long View Cider
Nine Pin Cider Works
Occam Fine Cider
Orchard Hill Cider Mill at Soons
Original Sin Cider
Quartz Rock Cider House
Stone Ridge Orchard
Treasury Cider
Vermont Cider Co. and Woodchuck Cider
Wayside Cider
and more
Discover cider’s remarkable range with outstanding bites. Cider’s nuances shine with food pairings, whether you’re trying something sweet or savory. Taste how complex flavors emerge when you try a sip of cider with nibbles from favorite local restaurants, chefs, and hot sauces like Achilles Heat Smoked Chili Crisp.

events.title: Beyond the Classic: Japanese YOUKOKU Relief Ceramics Exhibition by SUIYO @IPPIN Project
events.description:
Beyond the Classic: Japanese YOUKOKU Relief Ceramics Exhibition by SUIYO @IPPIN Project
[Introducing the Japanese YOUKOKU Relief Carving Ceramic Collection by Suiyo at IPPIN PROJECT]
Discover the captivating world of contemporary Japanese ceramics with the YOUKOKU Relief Carving Ceramic Collection by Suiyo, crafted in Aichi, Japan.
“As we’ve studied the classics, and with an eye on what will remain in the future, we will ‘go beyond’ images, genres, borders, and history, as well as our own past.”
— Daisuke Anayama
The collection showcases exquisite relief-carved ceramics featuring intricate motifs of auspicious animals, including cranes, turtles, and the animals of the Chinese Zodiac. Each piece brings together traditional Japanese craftsmanship and distinctive sculptural details, creating objects that are both meaningful and beautifully tactile.
Suiyo’s designs also draw inspiration from the classics of European art. In particular, Suiyo’s painter and carvener, Anayama Fumika’s designs reflects the decorative richness and intricate patterns of Austrian painter Gustav Klimt, creating a fascinating dialogue between Japanese ceramic traditions and European artistic heritage.
Experience a unique meeting of Eastern and Western cultural influences, where traditional craftsmanship goes beyond borders and is reimagined through a contemporary artistic lens.
Discover these beautifully crafted pieces at IPPIN PROJECT and bring a touch of Japanese artistry, symbolism, and timeless beauty to your collection.
*Artist: Daisuke Anayama: a ceramic artist and Fumika Anayama: a painter and carver.
Suiyo is a pottery brand produced by artists, Daisuke Anayama and Fumika Anayama based in Seto, Aichi. The brand concept “Beyond the Classic.” expresses their determination and hope to move forward to make their artworks a new classic in the modern age.

events.title: Industry City Gourmet Food and Drinks Tour
events.description:
Set against the iconic backdrop of Sunset Park’s historic waterfront, the massive, revitalized structures of Industry City form a breathtaking stage for an exclusive culinary journey. This premium food and cocktail tour is a curated exploration of taste and craft, transforming an evening into a memorable, high-end experience.
Your adventure begins with artistic bonbons at Lilac Chocolates, explores gourmet imports at Sahadi’s, and includes a refined whiskey tasting at Fort Hamilton Distillery, followed by a sophisticated sake flight. Savor additional artisanal discoveries within the awe-inspiring industrial halls.
Perfect as a distinctive date night, this tour is also fully customizable for private groups and corporate retreats. We specialize in tailoring this engaging experience for team-building and client entertainment, making it an ideal one-day corporate outing. A sophisticated mini-vacation for locals and a profound discovery for visitors.
